rationale: C24 plausibly supplied a material diplomatic-letter template: acknowledgment of a message conveyed through a senior intermediary, affirmation of historically close bilateral ties, declaration that the relationship should rest on sovereign equality, recognition of a sensitive dispute involving U.S. operations in the recipient country, and willingness to have the two governments' representatives conduct discussions. The child adapts that sequence and machinery to disagreements over Canal treaty rights and a forthcoming U.S. review. C09 and C15 share the child’s friendship-and-consultation framing, but lack C24’s concrete combination of disputed U.S. operations, equality between sovereign states, and proposed intergovernmental talks.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have read with great interest your [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] which your brother delivered to me... I am also very pleased to have had a personal conversation with your brother
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have been deeply interested in the Vice President's enthusiastic report... and of the wisdom and statesmanship with which you spoke on matters affecting the common interests of our two countries
shared_material.explanation: Both open by acknowledging a communication and substantive personal diplomacy conducted through a prominent intermediary.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Government of the United States hopes to maintain and strengthen the relations between our two nations on the basis of mutual respect and sincere friendship.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: we have always desired that our relationship be based on the only defensible basis, that of equality between two sovereign and independent states
shared_material.explanation: Both expressly define the normative basis for the bilateral relationship before addressing the dispute.

shared_material.child_excerpt: arrangements should be made to permit qualified representatives of both nations to discuss these points of dissatisfaction with a view to their resolution
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Government of the United States is prepared to participate in conversations on the subject of our military operations in Morocco... continued collaboration in examining this and other questions of mutual interest to our two countries
shared_material.explanation: The central administrative mechanism is materially parallel: representatives of two friendly sovereign governments are to discuss and resolve sensitive issues arising from a U.S. presence or operation in the other country.
